editorial:
Imagine being married to a man who looks like a hero but is actually a monster. You have a rich wife and a doctor husband who is obsessed with brain surgery. He does not love her; he just wants her money to fund his creepy lobotomy experiments. He spends the whole movie trying to trick her into thinking she is going crazy so he can put her on his operating table and kill her. It feels like a mean game of cat and mouse, but there is a spooky twist because a ghost from his past is watching everything. This ghost wants to save the wife and gives her clues to find out what her husband is really planning.

What makes this work is the creepy tension and the weird 80s vibe. The acting is a bit over the top, but that just adds to the fun of a low-budget horror flick. It moves along quickly, though some parts feel a bit choppy since different versions of the movie exist. If you love old-school thrillers with a supernatural kick, you should definitely check this out. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture, or just look for it to rent on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The movie ends when the wife finally realizes her husband is trying to kill her. The ghost of the previous victim helps her escape the operating room just in time. In a final twist, the evil doctor gets a taste of his own medicine. He ends up becoming a victim of the very brain surgery he used to hurt others. He loses his mind and spends his final moments trapped in the same madness he tried to force on his wife.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s B-movies and stories about evil doctors.
